items.limitation: Edits keep a correction history (earlier values and source); browser-tested with synthetic records

Owner-held encrypted files and the legacy vault remain separate from the staged revision runtime. Synthetic tests cover submission snapshots and interrupted-save readback. A readback clears an unsaved draft only if the exact submitted revision and checksum match and the payload decrypts successfully. No write is retried. Failed clean reopens remove the displayed copy. The fingerprint lasts for the authenticated tab session. The live Owner Desk does not load the staged runtime. Live owner recovery, cross-device revision integration and a durable rollback trust anchor remain unverified.

Encrypted workspace save, download, reload and restore were browser-tested with synthetic records. Tampered backups are refused. Staged encrypted revision backups support selected accounting sections and separately validated claim histories. Claim recovery preserves existing records and refuses divergent histories and reused payment references. A payment reference is an owner record and requires independent verification. Recovery creates an unsaved edit against the current verified head and preserves the Decision Spellchecker programme and server history. Other specialized evidence remains outside this recovery procedure. Owner recovery and backup provenance remain unverified.

CSV import skips duplicates; a manual entry matching an existing record's kind, date, amount and payer asks first, and unconfirmed repeats are reported as a completeness gap. Duplicates across different payees or amounts are not detected
Classes reflect owner-recorded evidence; no bank feed is connected
Reports are not accountant-reviewed and not tax-filing ready
Simulated in Chromium at 320, 375, 390 and 430 px; the hosted app has rendered on the owner's physical iPhone in Safari (screenshots, 2026-11-04), but form entry on the device has not been observed

items.limitation: The legacy vault and staged revision transport refuse HTTP redirects. Authentication requests are limited to the configured HTTPS Supabase origin. Workspace passphrases and plaintext records stay on the device. Tokens remain in page memory. Authenticated responses and local cryptographic handoffs are session-bound. The staged transport snapshots validated configuration, bounds token retrieval and sanitizes provider errors. Hosted response headers and exclusive live owner access remain unverified.

items.limitation: Superseded 2026-11-05: earlier text said server-side storage was a prepared, unapplied schema. Now: a separate free Supabase project (incomeos-private) holds only device-encrypted workspaces, append-only, readable only by an allow-listed owner; access rules verified in the database with anonymous and non-owner roles; client round trip tested against a fake service only. Free plan pauses after a week unused and has no automatic backups; the owner keeps file saves as backup Separate from that existing append-only vault, a server-authoritative compare-and-swap revision service is under development on an isolated branch. Its SQL has passed disposable PostgreSQL tests, and the encrypted workspace bridge has passed synthetic, real-crypto integration tests. It has not been migrated to the live database, enabled in the Owner Desk, or accepted through a real owner save-and-restore round trip. The staged accounting coordinator reuses the existing accountant's record validator and the authoritative workspace change log; synthetic tests verify conflicts, retained drafts, encrypted backups and explicit review. This evidence does not establish live hosted persistence, real owner authentication or owner acceptance. Staging-only runtime composition now uses the existing accountant, encrypted owner workspace and session-bound revision transport. Synthetic end-to-end tests cover concurrent edits, encrypted draft rescue, commit-then-timeout, sign-out during local encryption/decryption, and no unrequested writes. These results are not an authenticated production round trip or authorization to enable revision writes. The staged revision reliability soak exercises 120 deterministic concurrent-owner write races, denies 120 stale writes, checks commit-then-timeout recovery, ciphertext equivocation, rollback rejection, and no automatic writes. The browser vault now binds local encryption and decryption handoffs to the initiating owner session; sign-out revokes them and clears the entered passphrase, but an already loaded local workspace may remain visible until the page is closed or reloaded. These simulations do not replace real owner recovery, physical device acceptance, or a live server-authoritative revision migration. Same-session revision close now suspends editing authority without discarding the high-water revision, checksum history or an outstanding owner-review hold. Disposable PostgreSQL concurrency verification is rerun when revision clients change. The in-memory high-water protection does not persist across page reloads or a new device and is not an independent server audit. The owner acceptance protocol is documented in owner/incomeos/OWNER-ACCEPTANCE-PROTOCOL.md; it is a prospective test procedure, not completed acceptance evidence. Additional synthetic verification on 2026-11-08 covers finite session expiry, revocation on HTTP 401, expiry during hashing/requests, local draft revocation, bounded staged RPC response-body deadlines and sanitized service errors. In-memory preservation of an already loaded workspace is not secure tab erasure or independently verified owner recovery. Legacy vault HTTP deadlines and an uncertain-save hold now require an integrity-verified new read before another same-page save. This hold is memory-only and cannot replace the staged server CAS across page reloads or devices. No approved non-production Supabase management/database credential was available for migration in this session.
